scenarioStory.history: Wife reports three days of gradually worsening shortness of breath and bilateral leg swelling, with the patient sleeping upright in his recliner the past two nights because he can't breathe lying flat. Tonight his breathing suddenly worsened after dinner, becoming labored and audibly wet-sounding, prompting the 911 call.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 71-year-old male with a history of CHF sitting upright in a recliner in visible respiratory distress, with audible wet breath sounds and bilateral pedal edema. → CPAP initiated and coached: Crew escalates oxygen therapy to CPAP for severe respiratory distress from suspected pulmonary edema, coaching the patient through mask placement and titrating to target oxygenation. → CPAP seal maintained continuously: Continuous, uninterrupted CPAP further improves oxygenation and work of breathing. The patient is packaged and transported without breaking the mask seal.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Increasing shortness of breath and leg swelling

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 71-year-old male with a history of CHF sitting upright in a recliner in visible respiratory distress, with audible wet breath sounds and bilateral pedal edema.
relatedChecklist: Escalate therapy from supplemental O2 to CPAP for severe respiratory distress
Titrate oxygen/CPAP settings to target SpO2 94-98%
Coach and reassure patient through CPAP mask placement to achieve tolerance
Place waveform capnography in-line with CPAP to monitor ventilatory status

scenarioEvents.name: CPAP initiated and coached
scenarioEvents.description: Crew escalates oxygen therapy to CPAP for severe respiratory distress from suspected pulmonary edema, coaching the patient through mask placement and titrating to target oxygenation.
relatedChecklist: Maintain continuous, uninterrupted CPAP mask seal through transport to ED bedside

scenarioEvents.name: CPAP seal maintained continuously
scenarioEvents.description: Continuous, uninterrupted CPAP further improves oxygenation and work of breathing. The patient is packaged and transported without breaking the mask seal.
relatedChecklist: Reassess vital signs and work of breathing after CPAP; document response to therapy

scenarioEvents.name: CPAP seal broken en route
scenarioEvents.description: The crew breaks the CPAP mask seal during transport, causing an abrupt loss of positive pressure and rapid return of severe respiratory distress.
relatedChecklist: Immediately reapply CPAP mask and reestablish a continuous seal
